must_have_properties: Every wire-side Ethernet frame is a valid IEEE 802.3 frame (Preamble + SFD + DA + SA + EtherType + Payload + FCS).
EtherType field equals 0x88A4 (or UDP/IP encapsulation with dst port 0x88A4).
EtherCAT header has Type=0x1 (or 0x4 for EAP Network Variables) and Length consistent with the datagram block.
Each datagram has a valid 10-byte header + Data field + 2-byte Working Counter at the correct offsets.
SubDevices forward frames on-the-fly without store-and-forward delay; per-hop latency stays within ESC datasheet specification (typically <1500 ns at 100 Mb/s).
Working Counter is incremented per the spec rules (+1 read, +2 write, +3 read-write) by every addressed SubDevice.
ESM follows the 6-state model with only the legal transitions; AL Status reports the current state (or state+Error bit) honestly.
Process-Data Watchdog forces Op → SafeOp on cyclic frame loss.
Each ESC has hardware auto-loopback on any port without an active link partner.
SII EEPROM holds a valid ESI per ETG.2000; SII checksum is correct.
Mailbox SM channels enforce atomic write-then-read; SubDevice CPU cannot observe a half-written mailbox message.
Process-data SyncManager 3-buffer mode prevents PDI from reading a half-written buffer.
DC-capable SubDevices honor System Time Offset + System Time Delay; SYNC0/SYNC1 generation follows the configured cycle time.
must_not_have_properties: MUST NOT emit any wire-side Ethernet frame with malformed FCS that the ESC originated.
MUST NOT silently drop datagrams addressed to this SubDevice (must always update Working Counter on success OR leave it untouched).
MUST NOT autonomously transition out of Op except via PD WD expiry or MainDevice request.
MUST NOT modify bytes outside its addressed FMMU regions during LRD/LWR/LRW.
MUST NOT respond to mailbox protocols not declared in SII Mailbox Protocols bitmask.
MUST NOT allow MainDevice to enter Op without traversing PreOp + SafeOp first.
MUST NOT discard frames with unknown EtherCAT header Type — forward transparently.
MUST NOT reuse a Configured Station Address conflicting with another SubDevice on the same logical bus.
compliance_failure_modes: Conformance test fails on illegal ESM transition (e.g. Init → Op direct request) — SubDevice must report AL Status Code 0x0011.
Conformance test fails on Working Counter miscount — SubDevice must increment +1/+2/+3 per spec.
Conformance test fails on mailbox protocol response when protocol not declared in SII bitmask.
Conformance test fails on PD WD not expiring within configured window after cyclic frame loss.
Conformance test fails on DC SYNC0 jitter exceeding spec threshold (vendor-specific, typically <1 µs).
Conformance test fails on SII checksum mismatch on power-up reload.
Conformance test fails on frame forwarding error (e.g. corrupted bytes outside addressed region).
frame_boundary_compliance: ESC forwards every Ethernet frame that arrives on Port 0 (or any port set as 'open') to the next open port without altering bytes outside addressed-FMMU regions or addressed-register regions.
Frames with corrupted FCS are still forwarded (with corrupted FCS preserved) and counted in Frame Error Counter (0x0300).
Frames shorter than 60 B are not generated by SubDevices but may be received (padded by the originating MAC); processed normally.
address_filter_compliance: Destination MAC is NOT used to filter EtherCAT frames; every frame is processed for datagrams.
AP/FP/BC/LOG addressing is applied at the datagram level: SubDevice's match logic decides per-datagram whether to modify and increment WKC.
Multiple datagrams in one frame can address the same SubDevice with different Cmds; each operates independently.
reset_behavior_compliance: Hard reset → Init state; ESC re-reads SII EEPROM (or PDI-emulated SII).
Soft reset (via ESC Reset register 0x0040) → Init state; SII reload optional.
Hot reset (cable unplug + replug) → SubDevice's ESM state may persist (vendor-dependent); MainDevice sees AL Status via next BRD.
fields.min_link_constraint: Active link required on Port 0 for the SubDevice to participate in the network. Without link, the ESC is inaccessible from the wire; PDI access by local µC still works.
etg_certification_path: Apply for ETG membership (free for vendors)
Register a Vendor ID with the ETG (32-bit identifier)
Develop ESI XML descriptor per ETG.2000
Run ETG Conformance Test Tool (CTT) against the SubDevice
Submit conformance test report to ETG Test Center
Receive ETG.1500 Conformance Mark — visible badge on certified product
fields.safety_certification: FSoE (Safety over EtherCAT) products require additional certification per IEC 61784-3-12 + IEC 61508 SIL 3 (or equivalent ISO 13849 Cat 4 / PL e) by an accredited safety body (TÜV, exida, etc.).
